fills.researcher_notes: The wiki's '3 Billion cubic feet per day' figure is almost certainly a page-level/system-wide capacity number (consistent with Columbia Gas Transmission's overall interstate system throughput) mis-attributed to this specific Marysville Connector Pipeline row, which the sheet itself records as a 3.51 km (2.18 mile), 12-inch-diameter shelved lateral connector between Dublin and Marysville, Ohio. A 12-inch-diameter, ~2-mile lateral is physically incapable of carrying 3 Bcf/d -- that throughput requires large-diameter (30+ inch) long-haul trunk pipe, not a small local connector -- so I did not carry the wiki figure across; doing so would be a fabricated/implausible attribute. I searched for a project-specific capacity figure and did not find one: (1) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects table -- no Marysville/Dublin, Ohio connector project of this description located; (2) Ohio PUCO / Ohio Power Siting Board records -- no matching filing found under this project name; (3) FERC eLibrary-style search terms for 'Marysville Connector' / 'Dublin Marysville' Columbia Gas -- no distinct NGA-jurisdictional docket found (small local laterals of this kind are sometimes built under blanket certificate authority with minimal public docket detail, or may be state-jurisdictional); (4) a Columbus Dispatch (pressreader.com) article that appeared promising in search results returned HTTP 403 (paywalled) and could not be read even after re-attempting the fetch. Given the project is already marked 'shelved' and no independent, project-specific capacity figure could be located and verified, I am leaving Capacity UNRESOLVED rather than propose an unsupported or physically implausible number. A human with FERC eLibrary docket-search access or a subscription past the Columbus Dispatch paywall may be able to find a shelved-project capacity figure that this search could not reach.
